title: Asia's Traders Weigh Tech Selloff, US Midterms

notes.headline: Tech selloff deepens on AI monetization doubts, US midterms, and Middle East escalation risks
notes.summary: Global markets are grappling with a tech-led downturn as investors question the ROI and monetization timelines of massive AI capital expenditures, highlighted by disappointing guidance from Kioxia. Traders are bracing for the US midterm elections and the US Treasury refunding announcement, which carry significant implications for fiscal policy and bond yields. Meanwhile, central bank activity remains high with the BOJ signaling further hikes and the RBA expected to raise rates, while geopolitical tensions continue to support oil prices.
key_takeaways: AI monetization impatience and capex concerns are driving a significant selloff in global tech and semiconductor names.
US midterm elections serve as a major catalyst, with some analysts recommending buying the dip regardless of the outcome.
Goldman Sachs raised its December 2026 Brent crude forecast to $105/bbl due to substantial downside supply risks.
US Treasury refunding is a key focus, with speculation of reduced long-end auction sizes potentially flattening the yield curve.
Kioxia shares plunged after profit guidance missed estimates, signaling slowing NAND flash memory price growth.
Bank of Japan kept rates at 1.25% but signaled a December hike remains live as underlying inflation hits 2%.
Foxconn Chairman Young Liu defended AI demand as genuine and outstripping current capacity despite market skepticism.
OpenAI is reportedly seeking a $20 billion funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation while pursuing vertical integration.
macro: US midterm elections: Betting markets lean toward strong Democratic performance, while others eye fiscal gridlock as a bond market positive.
US Treasury quarterly refunding: Speculation centers on cuts to 20- and 30-year bond auction sizes.
RBA expected to deliver a 25 bps rate hike to 4.85% to counter persistent inflation.
BOJ Governor Ueda keeps a December rate hike in play following 2% underlying inflation milestone.
Middle East: Elevated risks as Iran threatens retaliation against potential US-Israel strikes.
China projected to lead in 8 of 17 strategic technologies by 2030, including robotics.
priced_in: RBA rate hike to 4.85% is largely baked into market expectations.
Betting markets price in strong performance for Democrats in the US midterms.
Market impatience regarding the return on investment for massive AI capital expenditures.
Potential cuts to long-end Treasury auction supply are not yet fully priced in.
fundamentals: Kioxia Holdings Corp: Guidance missed estimates (2.0T yen vs 2.35T yen expected) despite a 22-fold surge in quarterly profit.
Foxconn: Chairman states AI demand is real and enormous, justifying massive cloud service provider capex.
OpenAI: Pursuing vertical integration, including developing its own ASICs and IO devices.
China Robotics: Accounts for over half of the world's industrial robot installations in 2024.
Tech Earnings: Disappointments from Intel and Alphabet sparked concerns over infrastructure spending returns.

assets.view: Impatience over AI monetization and heavy short positioning create a volatile environment for tech.
Investors should buy the dip regardless of the midterm outcome as the event acts as a market clearing mechanism.
Brent price forecast raised to $105/bbl due to supply risks and geopolitical premia.
Treasuries are a safe haven; a split US government could limit fiscal spending and put downward pressure on yields.
The AI-driven selloff is bleeding into other sectors, including Japanese financials.

title: Big Tech Earnings Coming, Final Midterm Election Push

notes.headline: Big Tech earnings and US Midterms loom amid Strait of Hormuz disruptions and hawkish Fed

Geopolitical risks have spiked as Strait of Hormuz transit collapsed by 90% following vessel attacks, while Fed Chair Warsh maintains a hawkish stance despite softening late-Q3 consumer data. Investors are focused on whether upcoming reports from Apple and AMD can offset AI spending fatigue and persistent inflationary pressures.

Brent crude remains elevated above $113/bbl as Iran orders military readiness amid threats of strikes on energy infrastructure.
Quant trading firms like Citadel are paying up to $800,000 for AI PhDs to compete with tech labs.
BMO notes that a cooling in hyperscaler AI spending could actually assist the Fed's fight against inflation.
Brooks Running reports 12% revenue growth, suggesting the performance athletic consumer remains resilient.
macro: Fed Chair Warsh remains hawkish, viewing the economy as robust and requiring further work to reach inflation targets.
Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East impacts nearly a quarter of global oil transit via maritime choke points.

Midterm policy stakes include AI safety regulation, antitrust measures, and data center energy consumption.

Markets are pricing in the potential for a Fed rate hike in December.
AI spending fatigue is being priced in following negative reactions to Alphabet and Amazon results.
NYT/Sienna polls suggest Democrats are favored in several key states despite historical midterm trends.

Tech Earnings: High scrutiny on hyperscaler capex monetization for Apple, AMD, Palantir, Qualcomm, and Arm.

title: Tech Stocks Tank, Final Countdown to Midterm Elections

notes.headline: Tech Selloff Deepens on AI Capex Scrutiny and Midterm Election Headwinds
notes.summary: Megacap tech and semiconductor shares retreated sharply, with the Nasdaq 100 dropping nearly 3.5% and the S&P 500 falling 1.8%, driven by Intel's historic decline and mounting skepticism over returns on hyperscaler AI capex. The selloff spurred a rotation into defensive and duration-sensitive sectors as yields fell, though sticky inflation keeps the debate over Fed policy active. Geopolitical and policy uncertainty mounted ahead of the US midterm elections, with potential US-Israeli military action against Iran and Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries threatening crude supplies. Globally, Brazilian markets suffered a historic rout post-election on fears of fiscal expansion and debt growth under President Lula.
key_takeaways: Nasdaq 100 dropped 3.46% and S&P 500 fell 1.8%, breaching its 100-day moving average on heavy AI infrastructure capex scrutiny.
Intel plunged 28.6% in its steepest decline in decades following weak sales guidance and memory chip bottlenecks.
Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta declined as mounting AI capital commitments raised concerns over free cash flow and core business softening.
Crude markets face upside supply risks from potential US-Israel escalation against Iran and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries.
Falling yields buffered headline index losses, prompting rotation into defensive sectors while the Fed held rates steady amid sticky inflation.
US Midterm elections near with projections pointing to a split Congress, raising prospects of policy gridlock and increased oversight.
Brazilian assets crashed post-election, with the Ibovespa falling 18.3% and the real declining nearly 10% on fiscal sustainability concerns.
macro: Fed held interest rates steady as policymakers assess sticky cost-push inflation and energy pass-through risks ahead of the December meeting.
US midterm elections could split control of Congress, elevating legislative gridlock and shifting policy focus to executive actions.
Geopolitical escalation risks between the US, Israel, and Iran remain elevated post-midterms, threatening crude transport through the Strait of Hormuz.
Persistent consumer inflation in groceries, diesel, and mortgage rates continues to weigh on US economic sentiment.
Brazil faces heightened sovereign debt and fiscal deficit risks following President Lula's election victory.
priced_in: Markets had priced in smooth monetization from big-tech AI investments and heavy hyperscaler longs, triggering swift position unwinds.
Brazilian assets rapidly priced out pre-election optimism for pro-market fiscal consolidation.
Treasury markets are pricing policy uncertainty further out on the yield curve regarding Fed credibility.
fundamentals: Intel tumbled 28.58% to $65.76 following a weak sales outlook and severe memory chip supply constraints.
Alphabet and Amazon earnings signaled softening in traditional e-commerce and advertising, with margins pressured by AI spending.
Semiconductor index declined approximately 10% on hardware delivery timing and project execution bottlenecks.
Over 1,000 Ukrainian drones targeted three Russian oil refineries and a natural gas facility, disrupting processing capacity.
Binance suffered a $6.3 billion cyber heist, the largest cryptocurrency breach on record.

assets.view: Plunged 3.5% as heavy hyperscaler positioning unwound amid doubts over AI capex returns and semiconductor guidance cuts.
Fell 1.8% to break below its 100-day moving average, though downside was partially buffered by defensive sector rotation.
Crude prices face upside pressure from refinery disruptions in Russia and potential Middle East escalation impacting the Strait of Hormuz.
Falling yields supported duration-sensitive equities, but the yield curve steepened amid persistent inflation and uncertain Fed guidance.
Suffered a sharp rout as the Ibovespa dropped 18.3% and the real fell nearly 10% on post-election fiscal deficit concerns.

title: Israel’s Election Leaves Netanyahu in Limbo

notes.headline: Israel Election Deadlock and Potential Iran Conflict Heighten Geopolitical Risks Post-US Midterms
notes.summary: Israel's election resulted in no clear majority for Prime Minister Netanyahu or the opposition, potentially leading to months of political instability. This deadlock occurs as regional tensions with Iran are expected to intensify following the US midterm elections, with possibilities of joint Israel-US military action. Such geopolitical uncertainty could impact global energy markets and risk sentiment.
key_takeaways: Neither Netanyahu's Likud nor the opposition block secured a majority in the 120-seat parliament.
President Isaac Herzog will consult parties to determine who can form a coalition, a process that could take months.
Netanyahu's political survival is tied to his image as a security leader despite the October 7th failures.
Arab parties won a record 19 seats, complicating traditional coalition dynamics.
Ethan Bronner suggests a potential for military action against Iran after the US midterms, with a 10% chance before.
A military emergency could force a national unity government between Netanyahu and opposition leaders like Gantz and Bennett.
macro: Geopolitics: Political deadlock in Israel and potential for regional war with Iran.
Geopolitics: US-Israel military cooperation and its impact on Middle East stability.
priced_in: Expectations of a difficult path for any party trying to form a government in Israel.
Anticipation of increased military activity in the Middle East following the US midterm elections.
fundamentals: Crude Oil: Supply risks associated with potential military strikes on Iran or retaliatory actions.

assets.view: Potential for military operations against Iran could disrupt supply and drive prices higher.
Increased geopolitical risk and potential for regional war favor safe-haven assets.
Geopolitical instability in the Middle East typically weighs on global risk appetite.

guests.role: Israel Bureau Chief & Senior Mideast Editor, Bloomberg News
guests.key_view: Netanyahu faces a difficult path to a 61-seat majority, and the regional focus is shifting toward a potential conflict with Iran after the US midterms.

title: Midterm Fight Comes Down to the Final Days

notes.headline: US Midterm Elections Point to Potential House Flip and Increased Political Gridlock
notes.summary: The final countdown to the US midterm elections suggests a high probability of the House of Representatives flipping to Republican control, while the Senate remains a toss-up. Analysts discuss how a divided government would likely lead to a wave of congressional investigations and oversight into the administration's spending and personnel. Record-breaking early voting turnout, particularly in states like South Carolina, adds significant uncertainty to the final results.
key_takeaways: The House of Representatives is widely expected to flip to Republican control.
Senate control remains the primary uncertainty with key races in Alaska, Ohio, and the Carolinas.
A Republican-led House is expected to initiate aggressive oversight and potential impeachment proceedings.
Early voting is seeing massive surges, with South Carolina reporting an 83% increase over two years ago.
Donald Trump remains a polarizing but powerful driver of voter turnout for the Republican party.
Campaign financing has reached unprecedented levels, including significant 'AI spend' and donor activity from figures like Elon Musk.
macro: Fiscal gridlock is anticipated if the House flips, likely stalling major legislative agendas.
Increased geopolitical oversight is expected, specifically regarding foreign relations and administration spending.
Potential for administrative instability due to promised congressional investigations and impeachment attempts.
priced_in: Market consensus largely expects a Republican takeover of the House.
The Senate outcome is not fully priced in due to tight polling and high early-voter variability.
fundamentals: Massive campaign spending is noted, with Joe Mathieu highlighting 'AI spend' that is difficult to quantify.
Democratic candidates are raising significant cash, described as 'ATMs' for the party.

Significant 'AI spend' in the political cycle highlights sector relevance, though regulatory outlook remains tied to House control.

title: The AI Backlash Uniting Voters

notes.headline: AI backlash and data center resistance emerge as key political risks for tech infrastructure expansion
notes.summary: The discussion centers on the growing bipartisan backlash against AI, specifically regarding the construction of data centers and fears of job displacement. Local resistance to infrastructure is becoming a significant election issue, with some states like New York already issuing moratoriums. Despite these hurdles, experts argue that building AI capacity is a national security imperative to compete with China, likely leading to increased federal regulation and global standards.
key_takeaways: 61% of voters are against building more data centers due to concerns over noise, water, and land use.
New York has issued the first statewide moratorium on hyperscale data centers.
AI-aligned political groups have spent $56 million on elections to counter the backlash.
250,000 jobs in information services have been lost since the advent of ChatGPT, fueling voter anxiety.
CEOs and industry leaders are increasingly calling for a federal regulatory regime similar to the FAA for AI.
The tech race with China makes the continued build-out of AI infrastructure a strategic necessity despite local opposition.
macro: Geopolitics: The AI race is viewed as a competition against 'tyrannies like China,' making infrastructure a national security issue.
Labor: Significant job losses in the information services sector (250k) are driving political sentiment.
Fiscal/Regulatory: A proposed state-federal partnership would see states set infrastructure standards while Congress handles safety safeguards.
priced_in: Market expects continued massive investment in AI infrastructure, but may not fully price in local regulatory hurdles and moratoriums.
fundamentals: Hyperscalers face a 'PR problem' that is translating into political and legal barriers for data center expansion.
Information services sector is the most heavily impacted by AI-related job displacement thus far.

assets.view: Regulatory hurdles and local resistance to data centers could slow the growth of hyperscale tech firms.
Broad market impact depends on whether AI remains a 'job enhancer' or a 'job displacer' in the long term.

title: Haunted Attractions Help Revive Neighborhoods

notes.headline: Haunted attractions drive urban revitalization and seasonal consumer spending in neglected US neighborhoods
notes.summary: The segment explores how haunted houses have evolved from low-tech staples into elaborate immersive experiences that anchor urban renewal projects. These attractions draw significant crowds to previously neglected areas in cities like Baltimore and Kansas City, fostering secondary investments in infrastructure and retail. While primarily a seasonal business, the industry's growth reflects broader trends in consumer discretionary spending and niche real estate development.
key_takeaways: The US haunted attraction industry is estimated to include between 1,200 and 4,000 sites with paid admission.
Haunted houses are acting as catalysts for urban revitalization by funding local infrastructure like sidewalks and benches.
Attractions in cities like Kansas City and Salt Lake City have successfully drawn secondary businesses, including breweries, restaurants, and hotels, to industrial zones.
The industry is increasingly moving toward year-round monetization by hosting themed events for other holidays like Christmas.
Revenue is highly concentrated, with many operators earning their entire annual income over a few weekends in October.
macro: Localized urban economic growth and infrastructure development driven by niche entertainment sectors.
Trends in US consumer discretionary spending during the Q4 holiday season.
fundamentals: High seasonal revenue concentration for the entertainment and haunt industry.
Expansion of business models from seasonal to year-round operations to stabilize cash flow.

title: The Affordability Crisis Shaping US Elections

Inflation remains intolerably high, fueled by geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine alongside aggressive tariff policies. Experts debate the efficacy of the USMCA trade agreement and the regressive nature of recent fiscal measures as voters prioritize the cost of living.

Wages adjusted for inflation have remained flat or declined over the last two years.
